newsitem.title: Finland: Helsinki dips after global turmoil,seen recovering.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki dips after global turmoil,seen recovering.

text.p: * Shares end fair session down but off lows after Friday's global sell-off as a recovery on European markets and early gains in New York help Helsinki to cut losses. Brokers see scope for further recovery on Tuesday. Forestries strong.
* Vol FIM 373 million, .HEF +1.1 pct, .HEB -1.2 pct, .HEM -1.1 pct
Shares ended a fair Monday session down after Friday's global sell-off but off early lows as a recovery on European markets and early gains on Wall Street helped Helsinki to cut losses, brokers said.
"Our fall roughly corresponds to what overseas markets lost on Friday and gained today," one broker said.
Brokers said shares escaped the worst international turmoil after remarks by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan as Helsinki was closed on Friday for Finnish independence day.
The big decline was in fact felt in Nokia, while other shares held up better, they said.
The market was expected to continue recovering on Tuesday as markets were restoring confidence, brokers said.
"Nervousness seems to diminish, and I think we could see modest gains tomorrow," a broker said.
Nokia, which accounted for about 50 percent of the total volume on Monday, closed at 258.70 markka, down 7.30 markka for the day, but well above its 254.20 markka intra-session low.

Forestries bucked the trend and closed higher, helped by Norway's Norske's announcement that it expects pulp prices to rise at the beginning of 1997 and by Swedish Sodra's pulp price hike.-- Ilkka Virtanen, Helsinki newsroom +358-9-6805 0248
